phase_5c_comparison.methodology: Same stratified split (test=0.20, seed=42) on the v3 feature matrix (data/processed/features.csv). v2 uses its 30 feature columns; v3 uses 31. Both evaluated on identical 800 held-out test rows.

random_forest_v2.note: 30-feature model scored on the same v3 held-out test split (800 rows, includes technical certificates it never trained on).

random_forest_v3.note: 31-feature model on the identical v3 held-out test split.

v4_candidate_phase_6b.note: random_forest_v4 candidate scored on the SAME frozen 27-doc external set; identical to v3 (the workshop stratum did not change external results because all 27 frozen docs were already handled correctly).

phase_5c_comparison.reason: v3 generalizes to technical certificates (technical genuine recall 0% -> 100% on the frozen 27-PDF set) with suspicious recall held at 100% and zero false negatives. On the identical held-out split v3 raises accuracy 0.8425 -> 0.9287, precision 0.7083 -> 0.9422 and F1 0.7782 -> 0.8815 because v2 misclassifies ~91 genuine technical-certificate rows it never saw in training.

phase_6b_comparison.methodology: v4 candidate (trained on the v4 6-type dataset: academic/completion/training/online/technical/workshop, seed 42) scored on the SAME v4 held-out test split as v3, plus the frozen 27-doc external set.

workshop_stratum_666.note: rows the v3 model never saw in training (workshop type only existed from v4).

phase_6b_comparison.reason: v4 improves the workshop stratum (ROC-AUC 0.8755 -> 0.9457, F1 0.8389 -> 0.8475, FPR 0.0244 -> 0.0156) with zero added false negatives on the frozen set, but the frozen external validation is IDENTICAL to v3 (accuracy 0.963, FP=1, FN=0) and the identical overall test split is unchanged. Because v4 does not measurably improve the required generalization criteria and the frozen set is the acceptance gate, random_forest_v3 remains the active production model. random_forest_v4 is retained as a versioned candidate for roll-forward if real-world workshop documents arrive.

phase_6c_calibration_threshold.methodology: Threshold alternatives and probability calibration assessed on the v3 active model using a HELD-OUT validation split (600 rows) carved from the v4 processed features (fully out-of-distribution for v3; v3 was trained on the v2/v3 generation). Calibration (sigmoid/isotonic) was fit on the training split (2596 rows) via 3-fold CV ONLY, never on val or the frozen set. Frozen 27-doc external validation re-run after the change via run_generalization_validation.py env overrides.

candidate.training: isotonic calibration via CalibratedClassifierCV(cv=3) fit on training split only

external_validation.note: identical to v3; all 27 predictions unchanged

phase_6c_calibration_threshold.decision: No threshold change; no production calibration change. 0.5 retained as the decision boundary.
phase_6c_calibration_threshold.reason: (1) Threshold sweep on held-out validation shows 0.5 is already near-optimal: lowering to 0.30 reduces false negatives by only 3 (33 -> 30) while doubling false positives (9 -> 18) and cutting precision 0.9474 -> 0.9016; raising to 0.55/0.60 yields no gain. Per the priority (zero FN + acceptable precision), no single non-0.5 threshold is strictly better. (2) Calibration improves Brier (raw 0.0697 -> isotonic 0.0633) at a negligible AUC cost and changes ZERO predictions on the frozen 27-doc external set, but it is not an accuracy improvement and would change reported risk scores/confidence semantics for no decision benefit. random_forest_v4_calibrated is retained as a versioned candidate; the production model stays random_forest_v3 at threshold 0.5 with raw classifier probabilities. Reported risk scores remain PRELIMINARY AI estimates, not calibrated legal probabilities.

phase_5c_comparison.historical_benchmark: random_forest_vs_xgboost (below) was run on the v2 dataset and remains unchanged for record.
